name: Uchitaka
hype: Japanese sources (GetNavi's 東京・大衆酒場の名店 series, Tabelog matome, Retty) treat it as the benchmark shitamachi motsuyaki and nikomi counter, counted among the 'Tokyo five great nikomi', with queues before opening.
reality: Only score seen: Tabelog 3.91 in a 2013 ITmedia blog snippet, so it is dated and not re-verified live; no Google score seen.
tip: Cash only, closed Sundays and holidays, no reservations; queue before opening, order quickly (pork offal skewers, nikomi), eat and leave. Re-check the current Tabelog score before going. Keisei Tateishi station, 1 min walk.
baby_notes: Not for a baby: tiny standing-style, smoky, cramped queue-driven shop with a brisk 'eat and go' atmosphere; no stroller space.

name: KYOTO STAR BAR
hype: Selected as a Tabelog Bar Hyakumeiten (Top 100 Bars) in 2022 and reported at #36 on that list; a Pontocho branch of the Ginza STAR BAR, an authentic low-counter cocktail bar that also serves kakigori (shaved ice).
reality: Tabelog 3.68 from about 138 reviews (one page said 3.7 / 137 reviews); no Google rating seen. I could not confirm whether it still holds Hyakumeiten status in 2025/2026. Pontocho is touristy, so I am not marking it as a local pick.
price: Not verified; expect typical authentic-bar pricing (cocktails around 1,500-2,500 JPY) - unconfirmed
tip: Located in the 5th alley of Pontocho, about 244m from Sanjo Station. Opens late afternoon. Verify hours and reservation method on Tabelog before going. Try the cocktails and the natural-water kakigori.
baby_notes: Adults-only: a small counter-style cocktail bar in a Pontocho alley, not suited to a 5-month-old. Smoking policy not verified.

name: CHIKICHIKI Tenma
hype: Tabelog Yakitori Hyakumeiten (West) 2025 pick; casual sister of the high-end yakitori shop Goichi, grilling Tajima chicken.
reality: Tabelog 3.62 with about 468 reviews (listing page); an April 2024 review showed 3.70 so the score has drifted; no Google rating seen.
tip: Cash only, 30 seats, near Tenma Station (5-chome Tenjinbashi). Reserve ahead; Retty lists an up-to-JPY 8,000 all-you-can-eat-and-drink course. Confirm booking method on Tabelog.
baby_notes: Adults-only night out: lively yakitori counter/izakaya, alcohol-centered, not set up for a baby.

name: Stand Age
hype: Tabelog Standing Bar (Tachinomi) Hyakumeiten 2025 selection; hidden-away Fukushima bar with creative small dishes and a deep sake list.
reality: Tabelog 3.58 with 267 reviews per the Hyakumeiten list page; roughly 5 minutes from Fukushima Station; no Google rating seen.
tip: Standing is OK but not required; go early or midweek as small tachinomi bars fill fast. Order the creative seasonal dishes with sake.
baby_notes: Small standing bar, not suitable for a baby; keep for an adults-only night.

name: Kaisen Sosaku Kuriki
hype: Seafood izakaya and sake bar a short walk from Fukushima (Hanshin) Station, listed on Tabelog's Fukushima-ward ranking with a second branch for groups.
reality: Tabelog 3.53 seen on the Fukushima-ward list; review count and Google rating not seen, so the evidence is thinner than the other two.
tip: Address is Fukushima 1-3-16; groups up to 40 can use the second branch. Check Tabelog for current hours and booking.
baby_notes: Izakaya with sake focus; not verified as baby-friendly, treat as adults-only.

name: Hakone Onsen Tsurui no Yado Shiunso
name_ja: 箱根温泉 鶴井の宿 紫雲荘
hype: Japanese family-travel sites (いこーよ/icotto, Jalan, Rakuten Travel) list it as a baby-welcome Hakone ryokan with room dining and several private baths.
reality: Jalan overall rating 4.1 from 806 reviews; Rakuten features it for room-meal plus two kinds of private baths and 'three-generation trip with baby'.
price: approx 25,000-40,000 JPY per person with 2 meals (varies by plan/season)
tip: Book via Jalan/Rakuten or the official site and confirm baby goods (bouncer, bottle warmer) in advance as stock is limited. Paid open-air private bath 'Kanzan no Yu' sits across a suspension bridge; there is also a free indoor private bath. Tonosawa is quiet, short train ride from Hakone-Yumoto.
baby_notes: Room dining (部屋食), free private bath (貸切風呂), free baby goods loan (limited numbers), baby soap and baby bath chair lent at the main bath. Verify in advance that infant can use private bath and ask for bottle warming.

name: Kobe Arima Onsen Motoyu Ryusenkaku (baby room-dining inn)
name_ja: 神戸有馬温泉 元湯龍泉閣 〜赤ちゃんも楽しめるお部屋食の宿〜
hype: Marketed in Japanese booking sites (Jalan, Kinki Nippon Tourist, Nifty Onsen) specifically as a ryokan where babies enjoy room dining, with 50+ baby/kid services.
reality: Official and booking-site descriptions confirm room dinner, private open-air bath and baby services, but I found almost no actual guest review text, so quality is based on listed facilities.
price: approx 15,000-30,000 JPY per person with 2 meals (varies)
tip: Order the baby meal (離乳食) when booking. Private open-air baths such as 'Sakura' are reservation-based, so reserve slots at check-in. Free pick-up shuttle from Arima Onsen station; about 30-40 min by bus from Kobe/Osaka side routes.
baby_notes: Room dinner (部屋食), private open-air bath (貸切露天風呂), baby meal on order, free stroller loan, baby goods and kids yukata rental, indoor pool and kids corner. A 5-month-old with no solids may only need bath and room space, so the baby meal is optional.

name: Arima Onsen Miyukiso Hanamusubi (baby debut plan)
hype: Japanese travel-agency plan pages feature a dedicated 'baby overnight debut' plan for ages 0-2 at this Arima ryokan with gold-spring (金泉) baths.
reality: Seen only on Kinki Nippon Tourist plan listings; the plan bundles room meals, private gold-spring open-air bath, baby bath and free diaper changing. The plan as listed ran until 31 Oct 2026, so it must be re-confirmed for 2027. No review numbers seen.
price: approx 20,000-35,000 JPY per person with 2 meals (varies)
tip: Ask the ryokan directly whether the 0-2 baby debut plan is offered in your 2027 dates. Arima's kinsen (iron-rich gold water) can be strong, so check with the inn whether a 5-month-old should bathe in it.
baby_notes: Plan includes room dining (お部屋食), private gold-spring open-air bath (貸切露天風呂), baby bath tub and unlimited diaper changes. Confirm availability for 2027.

name: Hakone Yuryo
hype: Japanese travel and onsen sites (asoview, mapple, rurubu, iko-yo) repeatedly feature it as a secluded day-onsen with 19 private open-air rooms, among the largest such setups near Tokyo.
reality: No Tabelog or Google score seen (onsen, not food); I only saw descriptive Japanese listings, no review numbers, so the hype is editorial rather than verified ratings.
price: Adults about 1,700 yen weekday / 2,000 yen weekend; private room about 9,400 yen per 2 hours (2023 listing, check current)
tip: Reserve a private open-air room ahead; the main bath needs no booking. Free shuttle from Hakone-Yumoto station (about 3 min) or 5 min walk from Tonosawa station. Open roughly 10:00-20:00 (21:00 weekends/holidays). About 1.5 hours from Shinjuku by Romancecar.
baby_notes: Not for the baby: an adults-only evening/daytime outing while the other couple babysits. Private rooms let the two of you bathe without a crowd; tattoo rules are easier in private rooms.

name: Arima Onsen Kin no Yu (public bath)
hype: Japanese guides (jorudan, airtrip, rurubu, asoview) rank this public bath as the classic way to soak in Arima's rust-red, iron-rich kinsen water, and it is a long-standing Kansai favorite day-trip onsen.
reality: No Tabelog or Google score seen; Kobe city confirmed it reopened 17 Mar 2026 after renovation, open 8:00-22:00. It is a popular and busy public bath, so it is more classic than hidden.
price: About 650 yen weekday / 800 yen weekend; 2-bath combo ticket with Gin no Yu about 1,200 yen (listings, check current)
tip: Go on a weekday or late evening to avoid crowds. Closed on 2nd and 4th Tuesdays. Combine with Gin no Yu for the colorless water. Tattoo and towel rules apply; bring or buy a towel. About 1 hour from Osaka-Umeda by bus or train via Shin-Kobe.
baby_notes: Public same-sex baths, so no baby and no couple soaking together. Good as an adults-only evening trip while the other couple babysits.
